Path of the Totem Warrior.about: Your rage calls on the spirit of an animal, and you take on its strength and its ways. The hunters of the Emberwood and the high moors all tell stories about the spirit that walks with them.
features: Cast Beast Sense and Speak with Animals as rituals.

Pick an animal for your rage: Bear (resist all damage but psychic), Eagle (enemies have disadvantage on opportunity attacks; Dash as a bonus action), Wolf (allies have advantage on melee attacks against enemies within 5 ft of you), Elk or Tiger.
A lasting gift: Bear (double carrying capacity), Eagle (see a mile clearly, no penalty in dim light), Wolf (track at fast pace, stealth at normal pace), Elk or Tiger.
Cast Commune with Nature as a ritual.

A raging power: Bear (adjacent enemies have disadvantage attacking anyone but you), Eagle (fly while raging), Wolf (knock a Large or smaller creature prone with a bonus action after a hit), Elk or Tiger.

Path of the Ancestral Guardian.about: Your ancestors fight at your side when you rage, shielding the people you care about with ghostly hands. Families in [[Loreaon]]’s oldest quarters still keep the old names on their doors for this reason.
features: The first creature you hit each turn while raging has disadvantage on attacks against anyone but you, and anyone else it hits takes half damage, until your next turn.
While raging, use your reaction when an ally within 30 ft takes damage to reduce it by 2d6 (3d6 at 10th, 4d6 at 14th).
Cast Augury or Clairvoyance without spending mana, once per short or long rest.
Whatever Spirit Shield prevents is dealt back as force damage to the attacker.

Path of the Storm Herald.about: Your rage becomes a storm around you, shaped by the land you grew up in. Desert storms burn, sea gales strike, and tundra cold slows everything it touches.
features: While raging, a 10 ft aura: Desert (fire damage to creatures around you), Sea (lightning to one creature, Dex save half) or Tundra (temp HP to you and allies). Use it again with a bonus action each turn.
Resistance to your storm's damage type plus a small utility gift (no extreme heat or cold trouble, breathe and swim underwater, or freeze water).
Allies in your aura gain resistance to your storm's damage type.
Your aura bites back: Desert burns attackers, Sea knocks enemies prone, Tundra slows creatures to 0 speed.

Path of the Zealot.about: A god’s fury burns through you when you rage, and death itself struggles to hold you. Zealots of the church speak of the moment they came back from the dead, and the bishops are never quite sure what to make of it.
features: While raging, your first hit each turn deals extra radiant or necrotic damage: 1d6 + half your barbarian level.
Spells that bring you back to life need no material components.
Once per rage, reroll a failed saving throw.
Bonus action, once per long rest: up to ten creatures gain advantage on attacks and saves until your next turn.
While raging, you don't die at 0 HP; you fall only when the rage ends, if you're still at 0.

Path of the Beast.about: Your rage changes your body into something more animal: claws, jaws or a lashing tail. Those who fight beside you learn to keep their distance until the fight is over.
features: When you rage, grow a natural weapon: bite (heal a little when you hit while under half HP), claws (an extra claw attack), or tail (reaction to add to your AC against a hit).
Your natural weapons count as magical, and you choose a gift each rest: swim speed, climb speed, or a jumping boost.
When your natural weapon hits, the target saves (Wis) or must attack someone else or take psychic damage. A few times per long rest.
When you rage, up to your Con modifier allies gain extra damage once per turn while you gain temporary HP. Uses equal to proficiency bonus per long rest.

Path of Wild Magic.about: Wild magic surges out of you every time you rage, and no two surges are quite alike. Mages in [[Dragonsneck]] would pay a fortune to study you, and few of them would survive the study.
features: Sense spells and magic items within 60 ft as an action, a few times per long rest.
When you rage, roll on the Wild Magic table for a random magical effect (shadow tendrils, teleporting, a burst of light, a hungry spirit and so on).

Touch an ally to give them a d3 bonus to attacks and checks for 10 minutes, or to restore some of their mana: roll a d3 and they regain 5, 10 or 18 mana. Uses per long rest equal to proficiency bonus.
When you take damage or fail a save while raging, reroll your wild surge as a reaction.
Roll twice on the Wild Magic table and pick the result you want.

Path of the Giant.about: You grow with the strength of the giants when you rage, and you hurl your foes like stones. The quarry-folk of the high hills tell tales of barbarians who could throw a boulder over a river.
features: Learn Druidcraft or Thaumaturgy and the Giant language.
While raging you count as Large (if space allows), your reach grows by 5 ft, and thrown or Strength-based hits add more damage.
When you rage, infuse a weapon with acid, cold, fire, thunder or lightning; it deals an extra 1d6 of that type and returns to your hand when thrown.
As a bonus action while raging, hurl a Medium or smaller creature up to 30 ft (unwilling ones save).
While raging you can grow to Large or Huge, your reach grows further and your Elemental Cleaver damage rises to 2d6.

Battle Master.about: A tactician who fuels combat manoeuvres with superiority dice, and who wins fights by thinking three moves ahead. Captains of the Dornish Army train their officers in these techniques before they lead a single charge.
features: Learn three maneuvers and gain four d8 superiority dice, back on a short rest. Spend a die to trip, disarm, push, feint, parry, rally an ally and more. More maneuvers at 7th, 10th and 15th.
Study a creature for a minute to learn how it compares to you in two traits (Strength, AC, HP, class levels and so on).
If you roll initiative with no superiority dice left, regain one.

Eldritch Knight.about: A fighter who blends swordplay with abjuration and evocation magic. Knights who serve the great houses often take this path, learning enough magic to win a duel without giving up the sword.
features: Bond with up to two weapons: they can't be disarmed and you can summon one to your hand as a bonus action.

Your mana fuels a small wizard repertoire, mostly abjuration and evocation spells. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability. Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
When you cast a cantrip as an action, make one weapon attack as a bonus action.
A creature you hit has disadvantage on its next save against your spell before the end of your next turn.
When you Action Surge, teleport up to 30 ft.
When you cast a spell as an action, make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

Arcane Archer.about: An archer who weaves magic into arrows, and who can bend a shot around a shield or drop a monster with a single fletched bolt. The archers of the Garrison are famous for it.
features: Learn Arcana or Nature, and Prestidigitation or Druidcraft.

Know two Arcane Shot options (banishing, beguiling, bursting, grasping, piercing, seeking, shadow, enfeebling) and use them twice per short rest when you hit with an arrow. More options at 7th, 10th, 15th and 18th.
When you miss with a magic arrow, use a bonus action to reroll the attack against a different target within 60 ft.
If you roll initiative with no Arcane Shot uses left, regain one.

Cavalier.about: A mounted warrior and bodyguard who locks enemies in place and keeps the people beside them safe. Cavaliers guard the roads into [[Loreaon]] and ride with the nobles who pay for their steel.
features: One skill (Animal Handling, History, Insight, Performance or Persuasion) or a language.
Advantage on saves against falling off your mount, land on your feet if you fall, and mount or dismount cheaply.
Mark creatures you hit: they have disadvantage attacking anyone else, and if they do you can make a bonus action attack with extra damage.
Reaction: add 1d8 to an ally's AC against an attack, and give them resistance if it still hits.
Creatures that move within your reach provoke opportunity attacks, and a hit stops them in place.
Moving 10 ft straight before a hit can knock the target prone.
An extra reaction each round, only for opportunity attacks.

Samurai.about: Unshakeable resolve turns into precise, relentless strikes, and the samurai’s honour is the first thing they protect. Their courtly manners hide a deadly edge that few enemies see coming.
features: One skill (History, Insight, Performance or Persuasion) or a language.
Bonus action, three times per long rest: advantage on attacks this turn and some temporary HP.
Add Wisdom to Persuasion and gain Wisdom save proficiency (or another save if you have it).
If you roll initiative with no Fighting Spirit uses left, regain one.
Trade advantage on one attack for an extra attack.
When you drop to 0 HP, take an extra full turn before falling, once per long rest.

Echo Knight.about: You fight alongside an echo of yourself from another possible timeline, one that can attack, swap places with you and take blows meant for you. Some in the isles say the echo is simply the knight’s better self.
features: Summon a translucent echo (AC 14 + proficiency, 1 HP). You can attack from its space, swap places with it, and it makes opportunity attacks.
When you take the Attack action, make one extra attack through your echo. Uses equal to Con modifier per long rest.
See and hear through your echo, and send it up to 1,000 ft away.
Your echo throws itself in front of an attack meant for an ally, once per short rest.
When your echo is destroyed, gain temporary HP a few times per long rest.
Two echoes at once, and regain an Unleash Incarnation use when you roll initiative with none left.

Psi Warrior.about: Psionic power adds force to your blows and shields your allies from harm. Psi warriors are rare in the isles, and most of them keep their talents to themselves.
features: Psionic Energy dice (d6, rising with level), back on a long rest; regain one per short rest. Spend one to add force damage to a hit, cut damage to an ally, or move a creature or object with your mind.
Psi-powered leap (fly for a turn) and Telekinetic Thrust (push or knock prone with your force strikes).
Resistance to psychic damage; spend a die to end charm or fear on yourself.
Bonus action: give a few creatures half cover for a minute, once per long rest (or spend a die).
Cast Telekinesis without spending mana once per long rest (or spend a die), and attack as a bonus action while concentrating on it.

Rune Knight.about: Giant runes are carved into your gear, and you can grow huge when the fight calls for it. The smiths of [[Dragonsneck]] carve these runes for their best defenders.
features: Smith's tools and the Giant language.
Know two runes (cloud, fire, frost, stone, hill, storm) with a passive gift and an activated power each, once per short rest. More runes at 7th, 10th and 15th.
Bonus action: become Large for a minute, with advantage on Strength checks and saves and an extra 1d6 damage once per turn. Uses per long rest equal to proficiency bonus.
Reaction: force a creature to reroll an attack against an ally, a few times per long rest.
Grow a little taller permanently; Giant's Might damage rises to 1d8.
Use each rune's power twice per short rest.
Giant's Might makes you up to Huge, with 1d10 extra damage and more reach.

Way of Shadow.about: A ninja-like monk who moves between shadows and strikes from places no one expects. Shadow monks in the cities are often hired for jobs that never reach the watch.
features: Spend 2 ki to cast Darkness, Darkvision, Pass without Trace or Silence without spending mana; learn Minor Illusion.
In dim light or darkness, teleport 60 ft to another dark spot as a bonus action and gain advantage on your next melee attack.
Become invisible in dim light or darkness until you attack or cast.
Reaction: attack a creature within 5 ft that just got hit by someone else.

Way of the Four Elements.about: You channel ki into elemental disciplines, bending fire, water, earth and air to your will. Monks of the Four Elements are welcome in most temples, and most of them prefer the open road.
features: Learn Elemental Attunement and one discipline (more at 6th, 11th and 17th). Disciplines spend ki to produce effects like Fangs of the Fire Snake, Water Whip or Shape the Flowing River, some copying spells without spending mana.
Learn another discipline; you can swap one out when you gain a discipline.
Learn another discipline and spend more ki to empower them.

Way of the Long Death.about: A monk who studies death and feeds on it, and who finds strength in the last breath of an enemy. Other monks keep their distance from them, and the Grave Domain priests have their own opinions.
features: Touch of Death: When you reduce a creature within 5 ft of you to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your monk level plus your Wisdom modifier.
Hour of Reaping: As an action, a wave of dread sweeps out from you. Each creature within 30 ft must make a Wisdom save or become frightened of you until the end of your next turn.
Mastery of Death: Death's grip loosens for you. When you drop to 0 hit points, you can spend 1 ki point to drop to 1 hit point instead.

Touch of the Long Death: You can channel your ki into a killing touch. Spend 1 to 10 ki points, and a creature you touch takes 2d10 necrotic damage per ki point spent. It makes a Constitution save for half damage.

Way of the Sun Soul.about: You hurl ki as searing radiant light, and your strikes burn with the brightness of the dawn. Monks of the Sun Soul are often sent to the front of a holy war, and they count the days until they can rest.
features: A 30 ft ranged radiant attack that uses your martial arts die; can replace attacks and be used with Flurry.
After the Attack action, spend 2 ki to cast Burning Hands as a bonus action (more ki for a stronger version).
Action: a 20 ft radius burst of radiant light (Con save); spend ki to strengthen it.
Shed bright light, and creatures that hit you in melee take radiant damage.

Way of the Drunken Master.about: Lurching, staggering moves make you impossible to pin down, and your wine is never far from hand. The taverns of the port towns have a soft spot for these monks, and they always know who is buying the next round.
features: Flurry of Blows also gives you Disengage and +10 ft speed.
Stand up for 5 ft of movement, and redirect a missed melee attack to another creature.
Spend 2 ki to cancel disadvantage on a check, attack or save.
Flurry of Blows can make up to five attacks if each hits a different target.

Way of the Kensei.about: A weapon master whose chosen weapons become part of their martial arts. A kensei treats a blade as a sacred bond, and few are ever parted from theirs.
features: Pick kensei weapons that count as monk weapons, gain an AC bonus when you skip an attack, and add extra damage to ranged hits as a bonus action.
Your kensei weapons count as magical; spend ki for extra damage on a hit.
Spend up to 3 ki to give a kensei weapon that bonus to attack and damage for a minute.
Reroll a missed monk-weapon attack once per turn.

Way of the Astral Self.about: You summon your astral self: first spectral arms, then a visage, and finally a full spirit body that fights beside you. Astral monks say their guide comes from another plane, though few have seen it.
features: Spend 1 ki to summon spectral arms that strike using Wisdom with longer reach, and push enemies away when they appear.
Your astral face lets you see in magical darkness and speak with intimidating or quiet clarity.
With arms and visage out, deflect energy damage and add extra damage on a hit.
Spend 5 ki to manifest everything at once: AC bonus and an extra attack.

Way of Mercy.about: Healers and harbingers who carry both life and death in their hands. Mercy monks are the ones called to tend the wounded after a battle, and they are also the ones who end the suffering of the dying.
features: Insight and Medicine proficiency, and the herbalism kit.
Spend 1 ki to heal a creature with a martial arts die + Wisdom; can replace a Flurry strike.
Once per turn, spend 1 ki on a hit for extra necrotic damage.
Hand of Healing also cures a disease or condition; Hand of Harm can poison.
Replace each Flurry of Blows strike with Hand of Healing, and use Hand of Harm on one for free.
Spend 5 ki to bring back a creature that died in the last 24 hours, once per long rest.

Assassin.about: A killer who strikes first and from hiding, and who can vanish after a job without a trace. The guilds of the big cities pay assassins well, and the watch pays them even more to stay quiet.
features: Advantage against creatures that haven't acted yet in combat, and any hit on a surprised creature is a critical hit.
Spend a week and some gold to build a solid false identity.
Copy someone's speech, writing and mannerisms after studying them for three hours.
Hitting a surprised creature forces a Con save or doubles the damage.

Arcane Trickster.about: A rogue with enchantment and illusion magic, who makes a crowd forget what it saw. Arcane tricksters are welcome in the courts and feared in the taverns, and they can be both on the same night.
features: Your mana fuels a small wizard repertoire, mostly enchantment and illusion. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability. Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Your Mage Hand is invisible and can pick locks, plant or lift objects at range.
If you're hidden when you cast, the target has disadvantage on its save.
Bonus action: your mage hand distracts a creature, giving you advantage on attacks against it.
Reaction when a spell targets you: force a save to negate it and steal the spell for 8 hours, once per long rest.

Inquisitive.about: A detective who reads lies and finds the weak point in every story. Inquisitives serve the watch, the courts and private clients who cannot trust the official answer.
features: Insight rolls to spot lies treat a die below 8 as an 8.
Bonus action: Perception to spot hidden things or Investigation to find clues.
Bonus action: Insight against a target's Deception to gain Sneak Attack on it without advantage for a minute.
Advantage on Perception and Investigation if you move half speed or less.
Sense illusions, shapechangers and magic deception nearby, a few times per long rest.
Sneak Attack deals an extra 3d6 against a target you've read with Insightful Fighting.

Mastermind.about: A schemer who directs allies from the shadows, and who turns other people’s strengths into their own. Masterminds are rarely seen in the same room as the crime they planned.
features: A gaming set, a disguise kit, two languages, and the knack of mimicking accents.
Help as a bonus action, from up to 30 ft away.
Study a creature for a minute to learn how it compares to you in mental abilities and other traits.
Reaction: redirect an attack aimed at you to a creature giving you cover.
Your thoughts can't be read; you can feed false thoughts, and magic can't force the truth out of you.

Scout.about: A skirmisher and wilderness expert who moves quickly, sees everything and strikes when the enemy least expects it. Scouts guard the borders of [[Doresmere]] and the roads between the great houses.
features: Reaction: move half your speed when an enemy ends its turn next to you, without provoking.
Proficiency and expertise in Nature and Survival.
Advantage on initiative, and your first target in the first round is easier for everyone to hit.
A bonus action attack after the Attack action, which can Sneak Attack a different target.

Swashbuckler.about: A flashy duelist who darts in and out of combat with a grin and a flourish. Swashbucklers are the favourites of the taverns and the tavern-keepers’ daughters, and they are rarely short of a wager.
features: A creature you attack in melee can't make opportunity attacks against you that turn.
Add Charisma to initiative, and Sneak Attack a lone enemy in a one-on-one without advantage.
Persuasion against Insight: an enemy fixates on you (disadvantage on others) or a non-hostile creature is charmed.
Bonus action: advantage on your next Acrobatics or Athletics check this turn.
Reroll a missed attack with advantage, once per short rest.

Phantom.about: A rogue touched by death, who steals the knowledge and the last words of the dead. Phantoms are shunned by the church and tolerated by the Grave Domain, and they do not much care who approves.
features: After a rest, gain proficiency in a skill or tool of your choice.
After Sneak Attack, deal half the Sneak Attack dice as necrotic to another creature nearby. Uses per long rest equal to proficiency bonus.
Catch a soul trinket when someone dies nearby; use them for advantage on saves, extra wails, or to ask a spirit a question.
Become spectral for 10 minutes: fly slowly, pass through objects, attackers have disadvantage.
Wails from the Grave hits both targets with necrotic, and you always find a token after a rest if you have none.

Soulknife.about: Psionic blades formed from your mind cut through armour and thought alike. Soulknives are rare, and the few in the isles tend to keep to themselves.
features: Psionic Energy dice (d6, rising with level); spend them to boost failed checks or speak telepathically.
Manifest blades of psychic energy to make melee or thrown attacks, with a bonus action second blade.
Spend a die to turn a miss into a hit, or teleport with a thrown blade.
Become invisible for an hour, once per long rest (or spend a die).
A Sneak Attack with your blades can stun the target (Wis save), once per long rest (or spend dice).

Knowledge Domain.about: Priests of learning who know secrets, read minds and keep the old records. Knowledge clerics serve Korinth and are often found in the libraries of [[Akorsrest]].
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Two extra languages, and proficiency with double bonus in two of Arcana, History, Nature or Religion.
Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages
Gain proficiency in any skill or tool for 10 minutes.
Read a creature's surface thoughts (Wis save), then cast Suggestion on it without spending mana.
Add Wisdom to cleric cantrip damage.
Meditate to see recent events around an object you hold or the area you're in.

Light Domain.about: Bearers of fire and dawn who burn away darkness and the things that hide in it. Light clerics are the first to be sent when the night gets dangerous.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Reaction: impose disadvantage on an attack against you, Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
Dispel magical darkness and deal radiant damage to hostile creatures within 30 ft (Con save halves).
Warding Flare can protect allies too.
Add Wisdom to cleric cantrip damage.
Shed sunlight; enemies in it have disadvantage on saves against fire and radiant spells.

Nature Domain.about: Servants of the wild who charm beasts, shape plants and speak for the forests. Nature clerics are welcome in the villages and feared by the lumbermen.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Learn a druid cantrip and one of Animal Handling, Nature or Survival.
Channel Divinity: Charm Animals and Plants
Charm beasts and plant creatures within 30 ft for a minute (Wis save).
Reaction: give resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning or thunder damage to a creature within 30 ft.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra cold, fire or lightning damage (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).
Command charmed beasts and plants with a bonus action.

Tempest Domain.about: Storm priests who answer blows with thunder and lightning, and who see the sea as a holy thing. Thorum’s followers in the port towns speak of them with awe.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Reaction: a creature that hits you takes lightning or thunder damage (Dex save halves), Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
Make a lightning or thunder spell deal maximum damage.
Your lightning damage can push Large or smaller creatures 10 ft.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra thunder damage (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).
Fly at your walking speed when outdoors and not underground.

Trickery Domain.about: Tricksters who deceive with illusions and doubles, and who serve the god of mischief when the rules get in the way. Trickery clerics are good company until they are not.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Give a creature advantage on Stealth for an hour.
Create an illusory duplicate you can cast through, and gain advantage when you and it flank a creature.
Become invisible until the end of your next turn.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra poison damage (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).

War Domain.about: Champions of battle who strike with divine force and who believe every fight is a test of faith. War clerics ride with the knightly orders and fight in the front lines of every holy war.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Make a weapon attack as a bonus action after the Attack action, Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
+10 to an attack roll after you see the roll.
Reaction: give an ally +10 to an attack roll.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra damage of the weapon's type (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).
Resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

Forge Domain.about: Smith-priests who craft and wear the finest armour, and who believe the work of the hand is a prayer. Forge clerics are welcome in the great smithies of the isles.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
After a long rest, give a weapon or armor +1 until your next long rest.
An hour-long ritual to create a simple metal item worth up to 100 gp.
Resistance to fire, and +1 AC in heavy armor.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra fire damage (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).
Immunity to fire, and resistance to nonmagical weapon damage in heavy armor.

Grave Domain.about: Guardians against undeath who keep the dying alive and finish the doomed with mercy. Grave clerics walk the cemeteries of the old cities and keep watch over the dead.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Healing a creature at 0 HP uses maximum dice; Spare the Dying works at 30 ft as a bonus action.
Sense undead within 60 ft, Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
Channel Divinity: Path to the Grave
Curse a creature so the next attack against it deals double damage.
Reaction: turn a critical hit on you or an ally into a normal hit, Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
Add Wisdom to cleric cantrip damage.
When an enemy dies nearby, you or an ally regains HP equal to its Hit Dice.

Order Domain.about: Enforcers of law who command allies and punish disobedience. Order clerics serve the church’s courts and the king’s peace, and they expect obedience from everyone.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Heavy armor, and Intimidation or Persuasion.
When you cast a spell with mana on an ally, they can make one attack as a reaction.
Charm creatures of your choice within 30 ft until your next turn and make them drop what they hold (Wis save).
Cast enchantment spells as a bonus action, Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra psychic damage (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).
Mark a creature you hit; the next ally hit on it adds psychic damage.

Peace Domain.about: Peacemakers who bind allies together and calm the rage of a crowd. Peace clerics are often sent to settle disputes between the great houses.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Bond a few creatures: once per turn each can add a d4 to an attack, check or save while near another bonded creature.
Move without provoking and heal each creature you pass.
Bonded creatures can teleport to each other to take damage for one another.
Add Wisdom to cleric cantrip damage.
The bond reaches 60 ft, and the creature that takes the hit gains resistance.

Twilight Domain.about: Guardians of the in-between hours, who shield travellers from the dark and the things that walk in it. Twilight clerics keep the night watches at the gates of the isles.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Darkvision 300 ft, which you can share.
Give a creature advantage on its next initiative roll.
A sphere of dim light around you for a minute: each turn allies in it gain temporary HP or shake off charm or fear.
Fly in dim light or darkness for a minute, a few times per long rest.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra radiant damage (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).
Your sanctuary also gives half cover.

Arcana Domain.about: Scholars of magic who study the workings of the arcane and the divine together. Arcana clerics are sought out by mages who want a god’s blessing on their spells.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Arcana proficiency and two wizard cantrips.
Turn (and later banish) celestials, elementals, fey and fiends.
When you heal an ally with a spell, also end one spell on them.
Add Wisdom to cleric cantrip damage.
Add wizard spells of 6th to 9th level to your list (you still need the charges or channel to cast them).

Death Domain.about: Priests of the end of life who see death as a guide, not an enemy. Death clerics of Azrul keep the Bone Hall beneath [[Akorsrest]] and answer questions from the dead.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Learn a necromancy cantrip that can target two creatures next to each other.
Melee hit deals extra necrotic damage: 5 + twice your cleric level.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra necrotic damage (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).
Single-target necromancy spells of 1st to 5th level can target a second creature.

Oath of the Ancients.about: You keep the old oaths to the forests, the rivers and the gods of the land, and you protect the living world from those who would burn it. Druids and paladins of the Ancients speak to each other as old friends.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your oath's spells suit your vows; learn them from tomes or your order at the usual cost.
Spectral vines restrain a creature (Str or Dex save).
Turn fey and fiends, revealing their true forms.
You and allies within 10 ft have resistance to spell damage (30 ft at 18th).
Drop to 1 HP instead of 0 once per long rest, and you stop aging.
Transform for a minute, once per long rest: regain HP each turn, cast faster, and enemies nearby have disadvantage on saves against you.

Oath of Vengeance.about: You swear to hunt down those who have done great wrong, and you do not stop until the debt is paid. Vengeful paladins are welcome in the courts of justice and feared in the taverns of the guilty.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your oath's spells suit your vows; learn them from tomes or your order at the usual cost.
Frighten one creature and freeze its speed (Wis save).
Advantage on attacks against one creature for a minute.
After an opportunity attack hit, move half your speed without provoking.
Reaction: attack the target of your Vow of Enmity when it attacks.
Grow wings and a menacing aura for an hour, once per long rest.

Oathbreaker.about: A paladin who has broken their oath and now serves a darker cause. Oathbreakers are hunted by their old orders, and they have their own reasons for everything they do.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your oath's spells suit your vows; learn them from tomes or your order at the usual cost.
Take control of an undead creature (Wis save).
You and undead or fiends within 10 ft add Charisma to melee damage (30 ft at 18th).
Resistance to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing and slashing.
A minute-long aura of gloom that frightens and damages enemies, once per long rest.

Oath of Conquest.about: You swear to bring the enemy to heel and rule the lands you take. Conquest paladins are the iron fist of the great houses, and they remember every castle they ever took.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your oath's spells suit your vows; learn them from tomes or your order at the usual cost.
Frightened enemies within 10 ft can't move and take psychic damage (30 ft at 18th).
Creatures that hit you take psychic damage equal to your Charisma.
A minute of resistance to all damage, an extra attack and critical hits on 19–20, once per long rest.

Oath of Redemption.about: You swear to end fights without bloodshed where you can, and to give a second chance to those who have fallen. Redemption paladins are often sent to talk with rebels and bandits before the swords come out.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your oath's spells suit your vows; learn them from tomes or your order at the usual cost.
Reaction: a creature that hurts another takes radiant damage equal to what it dealt (Wis save halves).
Reaction: take the damage meant for an ally within 10 ft (30 ft at 18th).
Regain HP at the end of your turn while below half.
Resistance to all damage, and attackers take radiant damage back, unless you attack them.

Oath of Glory.about: You swear to live and die by deeds worth singing about. Glory paladins are the heroes of the taverns, and they are rarely careful about the cost of a good song.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your oath's spells suit your vows; learn them from tomes or your order at the usual cost.
Advantage on Athletics and Acrobatics, and bigger jumps and carrying, for 10 minutes.
After Divine Smite, share temporary HP among allies.
+10 ft speed, and allies who start near you move faster (aura grows at 18th).
Reaction: add Charisma to AC against an attack and strike back if it misses.
For a minute, once per long rest: advantage on Charisma checks, turn a miss into a hit once per turn, and reroll failed saves.

Oath of the Watchers.about: You swear to guard the people against the unnatural and the things that come out of the dark. Watchers keep the night patrols at the walls of [[Loreaon]] and at the lonely watchtowers beyond.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your oath's spells suit your vows; learn them from tomes or your order at the usual cost.
Allies gain advantage on Int, Wis and Cha saves for a minute.
Turn aberrations, celestials, elementals, fey and fiends.
You and allies add your proficiency bonus to initiative (aura grows at 18th).
Reaction: when an ally succeeds on a mental save, deal force damage to the creature that forced it.
For a minute, once per long rest: truesight, advantage on attacks against extraplanar creatures, and banish them on a hit.

The Archfey.about: Your patron is a powerful creature of the fey, who gives you gifts and asks for favours in return. Fey bargains are binding, and an archfey’s price is always higher than it first seems.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit your patron; your patron may teach them, as a debt.
Charm or frighten creatures in a 10 ft cube (Wis save), once per short rest.
When you take damage, turn invisible and teleport 60 ft, once per short rest.
Immune to charm, and turn charm attempts back on the caster.
Trap a creature in an illusory realm for a minute, once per short rest.

The Great Old One.about: Your patron is an alien mind from beyond the stars, and its knowledge fills your head like a flood. Few mortals survive long enough to learn what it truly wants.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit your patron; your patron may teach them, as a debt.
Speak telepathically to any creature within 30 ft.
Reaction: impose disadvantage on an attack; if it misses, gain advantage on your next attack against that creature. Once per short rest.
Your thoughts can't be read, resistance to psychic damage, and psychic attackers get hurt back.
Touch an incapacitated humanoid to charm it permanently and talk to it telepathically.

The Celestial.about: Your patron is a being of light, and its favours pour through you like sunshine. Celestial pact-holders are welcome in the churches, though the Akorian bishops watch them closely.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit your patron; your patron may teach them, as a debt.
A pool of d6s (1 + warlock level) to heal creatures at range with a bonus action. Back on a long rest.
Resistance to radiant damage; add Charisma to one fire or radiant spell damage roll.
Gain temporary HP after each rest, and give some to allies.
When you'd make a death save, spring back to half HP and blind nearby enemies with radiant light, once per long rest.

The Hexblade.about: Your patron is a blade of ancient power, and the steel you carry answers to your will. Hexblades are sought out by the knightly orders and avoided by everyone who has seen one fight.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit your patron; your patron may teach them, as a debt.
Curse a creature: extra damage equal to your proficiency, crits on 19–20, and heal when it dies. Once per short rest.
Medium armor, shields and martial weapons; use Charisma for attacks with a chosen weapon.
Raise a slain humanoid as a specter that serves you until your next long rest.
Attacks from your cursed target miss half the time (roll a d6, 4+ misses).
When your cursed target dies, move the curse to another creature.

The Fathomless.about: Your patron is a creature of the deep sea, and its tentacles and currents answer your call. Fathomless warlocks are most often found in the port towns of the coast, and the sailors are not sure whether to thank them or pray against them.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit your patron; your patron may teach them, as a debt.
Summon a spectral tentacle that lashes for cold damage and slows, as a bonus action. Uses per long rest equal to proficiency bonus.
Resistance to cold, and talk to anything underwater.
Your tentacle can shield an ally from damage.
Cast Evard's Black Tentacles without spending mana once per long rest, with temp HP and steady concentration.
Teleport yourself and up to five creatures to a body of water within a mile, once per short rest.

The Genie.about: Your patron is a genie of the elemental planes, bound to you by a bargain of wishes and words. Genie-pact warlocks make fine merchants and worse guests.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit your patron; your patron may teach them, as a debt.
A lamp, ring or bottle: retreat inside it for hours, and add extra elemental damage once per turn.
Resistance to your genie's damage type, and fly for 10 minutes a few times per long rest.
Bring up to five creatures into your vessel; a short rest there heals more.
Once per long-ish rest (1d4 long rests), cast any 6th-level or lower spell with a casting time of one action, without needing a tome. Your patron will remember the favor.

The Undead.about: Your patron is a creature of death, and its gifts give you a grip on the grave. Undead-pact warlocks are feared by the church and sought by the cults of the dead.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit your patron; your patron may teach them, as a debt.
Bonus action: transform for a minute, gaining temporary HP and immunity to fear, and your first hit each turn can frighten. Uses per long rest equal to proficiency bonus.
No need to eat, drink or breathe; once per turn, an attack can deal necrotic and extra damage in your dread form.
Resistance (immunity in dread form) to necrotic; once per long rest, burst back to 1 HP when you'd drop.
Project your spirit for an hour: fly, pass through objects and resist physical damage.

College of Valor.about: Bards who sing of battle and stand beside the people they celebrate. The College of Valor sends its members to the front lines with a song in their throat and a shield on their arm.
features: Bonus Proficiencies: You train for the battlefield. You gain proficiency with medium armor, shields and martial weapons.
Combat Inspiration: Your Bardic Inspiration now lifts your allies in battle. An ally who has your Bardic Inspiration die can add it to a damage roll, or to its AC against one attack.
Extra Attack: You can strike twice in one turn. Attack twice whenever you take the Attack action.
Battle Magic: You weave spells into your strikes. When you cast a spell as an action, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

College of Glamour.about: Bards of fey enchantment, who sing of the wild courts and the beauty that hides their cruelty. Glamour bards are welcome at the balls of the great houses, and they leave every guest wanting more.
features: Spend Bardic Inspiration to give allies temporary HP and a free move without provoking.
After performing for a minute, charm a few listeners for an hour (Wis save).
For a minute, cast Command as a bonus action each turn without spending mana. Once per long rest.
Attackers must save (Cha) or choose a new target, once per short rest.

College of Swords.about: Bards who dance with a blade, combining swordplay with the rhythm of a song. Sword bards hold the stage in the taverns and the arenas.
features: Medium armor and the scimitar; use a weapon as your focus.
+10 ft speed when you attack, and spend Bardic Inspiration on a hit for a flourish: Defensive (add to AC), Slashing (hit a second creature) or Mobile (push the target).
Attack twice when you take the Attack action.
Use a d6 for a flourish instead of spending Bardic Inspiration.

College of Whispers.about: Bards who trade in secrets, rumours and quiet threats. Whisper bards are the spies of the bardic world, and they know which songs to sing to get a man to talk.
features: Spend Bardic Inspiration on a hit for extra psychic damage (2d6, more at higher levels).
Talk to someone alone for a minute and frighten them for an hour (Wis save).
Capture the shadow of a humanoid who dies near you and wear its persona as a disguise.
Whisper to a creature to charm it into obeying you for 8 hours (Wis save), once per long rest.

College of Creation.about: Bards who sing the world into being, and who believe a good song can change the shape of a room. Creation bards are often sought out by the craftsmen of the cities.
features: Your Bardic Inspiration carries a mote with an extra effect on checks, attacks or saves.
Create a nonmagical object worth up to 20 gp × bard level, once per long rest (or spend 10 mana to do it again).
Animate a Large or smaller object as a dancing companion, once per long rest (or spend 18 mana).
Create several objects at once with Performance of Creation, with no gold limit.

College of Eloquence.about: Bards who speak with perfect words and perfect timing, and who can talk a crowd out of anger or into a fight. Eloquent bards are rare, and the courts love them.
features: Persuasion and Deception rolls below 10 count as 10.
Spend Bardic Inspiration to subtract the roll from a creature's next save.
A creature keeps your Bardic Inspiration die if the roll fails.
Make a few creatures understand you for an hour, once per long rest (or spend 5 mana).
When a creature succeeds with your inspiration, give another creature a free die.

College of Spirits.about: Bards who call up the spirits of the dead through their song, and who listen to what the dead have to say. Spirit bards often find work in the cemeteries and the old battlefields.
features: Use a candle, crystal ball, skull or tarot deck as your focus, and later add a d6 to spell damage or healing.
Spend Bardic Inspiration to draw a spirit tale with a random effect you can use later.
An hour-long ritual with allies to learn a divination or necromancy spell temporarily.
Roll twice for Tales from Beyond and choose.

Circle of the Moon.about: Druids who take on the forms of beasts under the light of the moon, and who fight as fiercely as any animal. Moon druids are respected by the hunters and feared by the herders.
features: Wild Shape as a bonus action, and while transformed spend mana to heal 1d8 per spell level of that mana (5 mana heals 1d8, 10 heals 2d8, 18 heals 3d8, and so on).
Turn into tougher beasts: up to CR 1 at 2nd, then CR equal to a third of your druid level from 6th.
Your beast attacks count as magical.
Spend two Wild Shape uses to become an air, earth, fire or water elemental.
Cast Alter Self at will, without spending mana.

Circle of Dreams.about: Druids who walk the dreams of the forest and speak to the fey in their sleep. Dream druids are welcome in the fey woods, and they sometimes forget to come back.
features: A pool of d6s (equal to druid level) to heal and give temporary HP with a bonus action.
During a rest, make a 30 ft sphere that hides and shelters your group.
Teleport 60 ft as a bonus action (or teleport a willing ally 30 ft), Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
After a short rest, cast Dream, Scrying or Teleportation Circle without spending mana, once per long rest.

Circle of the Shepherd.about: Druids who call on the spirits of the land and its beasts to guard their people. Shepherds keep the herds safe on the high pastures and the roads.
features: Speak with beasts and learn Sylvan.
Summon a spirit for a minute: Bear (temporary HP, advantage on Strength), Hawk (advantage on attacks with your reaction) or Unicorn (better healing and finding creatures). Once per short rest.
Beasts and fey you summon have extra HP and magical attacks.
Your summoned creatures heal at the end of their turns in your totem's aura.
When you drop to 0 HP, four beasts appear to protect you, once per long rest.

Circle of Spores.about: Druids who work with fungi and rot, turning death into a new kind of life. Spore druids are unwelcome in most villages, and they like it that way.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Reaction: deal necrotic damage to a creature that moves near you or starts its turn there (Con save).
Spend a Wild Shape use for temporary HP and stronger spores and melee necrotic damage.
Raise a beast or humanoid that dies near you as a zombie for an hour.
Throw your spore cloud into an area instead.
Immune to blinded, deafened, frightened and poisoned, and critical hits become normal hits.

Circle of Stars.about: Druids who read the constellations and draw their power from the night sky. Star druids are the astrologers of the wild, and they are often consulted before a voyage.
features: Learn Guidance, and cast Guiding Bolt without spending mana a few times per long rest.
Spend a Wild Shape use to become a constellation: Archer (radiant bolt), Chalice (heal extra when you heal), or Dragon (rolls below 10 on Int/Wis checks and concentration count as 10).
After a rest, gain weal or woe: add or subtract a d6 to others' rolls a few times.
Starry Form gets stronger, and you can switch constellations each turn.
In Starry Form, resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing.

Circle of Wildfire.about: Druids who work with flame and ash, and who believe fire renews the land. Wildfire druids are welcome in the burned country and avoided in the dry woods.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Spend a Wild Shape use to summon a fiery spirit that fights and can teleport you and allies.
Add a d8 to fire damage or healing spells while your spirit is out, and cast through it.
When a creature dies near your spirit, leave a flame you can use to heal or burn.
If you drop to 0 HP, your spirit sacrifices itself to bring you back to half HP.

Beast Master.about: A ranger who fights alongside a loyal beast, and who knows the wild as well as any animal does. Beast masters are often found on the edge of the settled lands, where their companions are needed most.
features: Ranger's Companion: You bond with a beast that fights beside you and obeys your commands. You may choose a primal beast of land, sea or sky instead, keeping the bond you form in the wild.
Exceptional Training: Your companion learns to fight as a partner. As a bonus action, it can Dash, Disengage or Help, and its attacks count as magical.
Bestial Fury: Your companion's wild strength takes over in a fight. It can attack twice whenever it takes the Attack action.
Share Spells: Your companion shares the magic you cast on yourself. Spells you cast on yourself also affect the companion while it is within range of you.

Gloom Stalker.about: A ranger who hunts in the dark and strikes from the shadows, and who is most at home in the night. Gloom stalkers are the watchers at the edge of the dark places.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Add Wisdom to initiative, and on your first turn move faster and make an extra attack with extra damage.
Darkvision, and creatures relying on darkvision can't see you in darkness.
Proficiency in Wisdom saves (or another save).
Once per turn, when you miss, make another attack.
Reaction: impose disadvantage on an attack against you.

Horizon Walker.about: A ranger who guards the borders between the planes and the lands they know well. Horizon walkers see things that others do not, and they like it when others don’t ask about it.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Sense the nearest planar portal within a mile, once per short rest.
Bonus action: your next hit on a creature deals force damage and an extra 1d8 (2d8 at 11th).
Step into the Ethereal Plane for a turn, once per short rest.
Teleport 10 ft before each attack, and attack a third target if you hit two.
Reaction: gain resistance to an attack's damage.

Monster Slayer.about: A ranger who hunts the dangerous creatures that prey on the living, and who has learned their weaknesses. Monster slayers are paid well by the villages and the great houses alike.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Learn a creature's immunities, resistances and vulnerabilities, Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
Mark a creature: your first hit on it each turn deals an extra 1d6.
Add a d6 to saves and grapple escapes against your prey.
Reaction: stop a creature casting a spell or teleporting (Wis save), once per short rest.
Reaction: when your prey forces a save, attack it; a hit makes you succeed.

Fey Wanderer.about: A ranger who walks in the fey woods and carries a little of their magic. Fey wanderers are welcome in the wild courts, and they are cautious about the bargains they make there.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals an extra 1d4 psychic (1d6 at 11th).
Add Wisdom to Charisma checks, and gain one social skill.
Advantage against charm and fear, and redirect those effects at others.
Cast Summon Fey without spending mana once per long rest, without concentration if you choose a shorter duration.
Cast Misty Step without spending mana a few times, and take an ally with you.

Swarmkeeper.about: A ranger who commands a swarm of tiny creatures, and who hears them whisper what they have seen. Swarmkeepers are easy to find in the marshes and hard to surprise anywhere.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Once per turn on a hit, your swarm deals 1d6 extra piercing, pushes the target, or moves you.
Fly slowly on your swarm for a minute, a few times per long rest.
Swarm damage grows to 1d8, and its push knocks prone or its move gives you half cover.
Reaction: gain resistance and teleport 30 ft as you scatter into the swarm.

Drakewarden.about: A ranger who raises and rides a young dragon, and who has bonded with it for life. Drakewardens are rare, and the lords of [[Dragonsneck]] would like to know how they do it.
features: Summon a drake that fights beside you and grows with you.
Your drake grows, can carry you while flying, and you gain resistance to its damage type.
Breathe a cone of your drake's element (or command the drake to), once per long rest (or spend 18 mana).
The drake grows to Large, hits harder, and can shield you from damage.

Wild Magic.about: Your magic is unstable and surges out of you in strange ways. Wild mages are watched by the churches and the mage-guilds, who cannot agree on whether they are a blessing or a danger.
features: After casting a spell with mana, the DM can have you roll for a random wild magic effect.
Gain advantage on one roll; regain it on a long rest or when the DM triggers a surge.
Spend 2 sorcery points to add or subtract a d4 from someone else's roll.
Roll twice on the surge table and choose.
When you roll maximum on a damage die, roll it again and add it, once per turn.

Divine Soul.about: Your magic comes from the gods, and you carry a spark of the divine in your blood. Divine souls are welcome in the temples, though not always in the councils.
features: Learn spells from the cleric list as well as the sorcerer list, and gain one affinity spell (good, evil, law, chaos or neutrality).
Add 2d4 to a failed save or missed attack, once per short rest.
Spend 1 sorcery point to reroll healing dice.
Regain half your HP as a bonus action when below half, once per long rest.

Shadow Magic.about: Your magic draws on the darkness and the things that live in it. Shadow sorcerers are feared in the cities and useful in the places the watch cannot reach.
features: Darkvision 120 ft, and cast Darkness with 2 sorcery points (you can see through it).
When you'd drop to 0 HP, Cha save to stay at 1 HP, once per long rest.
Spend 3 sorcery points to summon a shadow hound that hunts a target and makes it worse at saving against your spells.
In dim light or darkness, teleport 120 ft as a bonus action.
Spend 6 sorcery points to become shadowy for a minute: resist most damage and move through objects.

Storm Sorcery.about: Your magic is the storm itself, and the wind and waves answer your call. Storm sorcerers are sought out by sailors and avoided by the captains who want their ships to stay afloat.
features: Fly 10 ft without provoking after casting a spell with mana.
Resistance to lightning and thunder, and a burst of storm damage when you cast those spells.
Control rain and wind around you.
Reaction: lightning damage and a push against a creature that hits you in melee.
Immune to lightning and thunder, fly 60 ft, and share flight with allies for an hour.

Aberrant Mind.about: Your magic comes from an alien mind that has touched your own, and its thoughts leak into yours. Aberrant sorcerers are unsettling company, and the scholars want to study them.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Link minds with a creature to talk telepathically.
Cast your psionic spells with sorcery points instead of mana, with no components.
Resistance to psychic, advantage against charm and fear.
Spend sorcery points for strange gifts: see invisible, fly, swim and breathe water, or squeeze through tiny gaps.
Teleport and pull creatures where you left with force damage, once per long rest (or 5 sorcery points).

Clockwork Soul.about: Your magic comes from the order of the cosmos, and you feel the gears of the world turning. Clockwork sorcerers keep the balance of the isles, and they dislike disorder of any kind.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Reaction: cancel advantage or disadvantage on a roll nearby, Proficiency-bonus times per long rest.
Spend sorcery points to give a creature a ward of d8s that soaks damage.
For a minute, attacks against you can't have advantage and your rolls below 10 count as 10, once per long rest.
Summon spirits of order to heal, repair and end spells, once per long rest.

School of Abjuration.about: Wizards who learn to protect, banish and shield, and who build wards that keep the dangerous out. Abjurers are the first hired to guard the great houses.
features: Copying abjuration spells costs half the gold and time.
When you cast an abjuration spell with mana, you make a ward that absorbs damage, recharged by more abjuration spells.
Use your ward to absorb damage for an ally nearby.
Add your proficiency bonus to ability checks made with abjuration spells (like Counterspell and Dispel Magic).
Advantage on saves against spells and resistance to spell damage.

School of Conjuration.about: Wizards who summon and transport things across the world, and who can bring a friend or a foe to their side in a heartbeat. Conjurers are the couriers of the mage-guilds.
features: Copying conjuration spells costs half the gold and time.
Conjure a small nonmagical object for an hour.
Teleport 30 ft, or swap places with an ally, once per long rest (or after casting a conjuration spell).
Damage can't break your concentration on conjuration spells.
Creatures you summon get 30 temporary HP.

School of Divination.about: Wizards who see the future and the hidden truth, and who read the signs that others miss. Diviners are consulted by lords before they make a choice.
features: Copying divination spells costs half the gold and time.
After a long rest, roll two d20s and keep them; replace any roll you see with one (three dice at 14th).
When you cast a divination spell of 2nd level or higher with mana, regain the mana cost of a spell one level lower (up to 40, a 5th-level spell).
Gain darkvision, ethereal sight, the ability to read any language, or see invisible things until your next rest.

School of Enchantment.about: Wizards who bend minds and charm people, and who can make a crowd agree with them. Enchanters are welcome at court and watched closely by the church.
features: Copying enchantment spells costs half the gold and time.
Charm a creature next to you and leave it dazed while you hold its gaze.
Reaction: force an attacker to target someone else (Wis save).
Single-target enchantment spells can target a second creature.
Make a creature you charmed forget it was charmed and lose some hours of memory.

School of Illusion.about: Wizards who make the world look like something it is not, and who can hide an army in a single room. Illusionists are the best liars in the isles.
features: Illusion Savant: You have a gift for copying illusion spells. Copying an illusion spell into your spellbook costs half the usual gold and time.
Improved Minor Illusion: Your Minor Illusion now makes both a sound and an image, so one cantrip can fool more than one sense.
Malleable Illusions: You can reshape an illusion you are maintaining. As an action, change the appearance of an illusion you have created and are concentrating on.
Illusory Self: Reaction: when a creature attacks you, an illusory double appears and makes the attack miss. You can use this once per short rest.
Illusory Reality: You can make a piece of your illusion real. Choose one non-living object within your illusion; it becomes real for one minute.

School of Necromancy.about: Wizards who study death and bring the dead back for a time. Necromancers are hunted by the church and sought by the desperate.
features: Necromancy Savant: You copy necromancy spells with ease. Copying a necromancy spell into your spellbook costs half the usual gold and time.

Grim Harvest: You feed on the death you cause. When you kill a creature with a spell, regain hit points equal to twice the spell's level, or three times if the spell is a necromancy spell of 1st level or higher.
Undead Thralls: Your dead serve you better. Animate Dead raises one extra creature, and the undead you create gain bonus hit points.
Inured to Undeath: Death no longer frightens you. You gain resistance to necrotic damage, and your hit point maximum can't be reduced.
Command Undead: You take command of the dead. As an action, choose an undead creature you can see within 60 ft; it must make a Charisma save or become your ally until you lose control of it.

School of Transmutation.about: Wizards who change one thing into another, and who believe any substance can be reshaped with the right words. Transmuters are the alchemists of the mage-guilds.
features: Copying transmutation spells costs half the gold and time.
Change one material into another (wood, stone, iron, copper or silver) for an hour.
Make a stone that gives darkvision, speed, a save proficiency or a resistance.
Cast Polymorph on yourself without spending mana, once per short rest.
Destroy your stone for a big effect: transform an object, cure everything, cast Raise Dead, or restore youth.

Bladesinging.about: Wizards who fight with a blade and a spell at once, dancing through combat with a song of their own. Bladesingers are the duellists of the elven courts and the wizard schools.
features: Light armor, one one-handed melee weapon, and Performance.
Bonus action, a few times per long rest: add Intelligence to AC and concentration saves, move faster, and gain advantage on Acrobatics.
Attack twice, and replace one attack with a cantrip.
Reaction while your Bladesong is active: spend mana to cut damage by 5 per spell level of that mana (5 mana cuts 5, 10 cuts 10, 18 cuts 15, and so on).
Add Intelligence to melee weapon damage while your Bladesong is active.

War Magic.about: Wizards who fight in the front lines and cast their spells with the blade. War mages serve the armies of the great houses, and they are the first to be wounded.
features: Arcane Deflection: Reaction: when a creature you can see hits you or a creature within 10 ft, gain +2 AC or +4 to a save. You can only cast cantrips on your next turn.
Tactical Wit: You read the field the moment a fight starts. Add your Intelligence modifier to your initiative.
Power Surge: When you counter or dispel a spell, you store a surge of raw force. Spend stored surges to add extra force damage to your spells, and the surges fade at the end of a long rest.
Durable Magic: Your concentration is hardened by years of fighting while casting. You gain +2 AC and +2 to saving throws while you concentrate on a spell.
Deflecting Shroud: Arcane Deflection now also bursts outward. Creatures within 10 ft of you take force damage when you use it, so your deflection becomes a counterattack.

Chronurgy Magic.about: Wizards who bend time for a moment, and who see the past and the future in a single breath. Chronurgists are rare and cautious, and the wise do not ask them to rush.
features: Reaction: force a creature to reroll an attack, check or save, twice per long rest.
Freeze a Large or smaller creature in time (Con save), a few times per long rest.
Store a 4th-level or lower spell in a bead someone else can use, once per short rest.
Decide whether a roll you can see succeeds or fails, at the cost of a level of exhaustion.

Graviturgy Magic.about: Wizards who shape gravity itself, dragging foes to the ground and lifting the heavy as if they were light. Graviturgists are feared for their power and respected for their care.
features: Adjust Density: You bend the weight of a creature. As an action, make a creature heavier or lighter for one minute, changing how far it can move and how hard it hits the ground.
Gravity Well: Your spells pull their targets along with them. When a spell you cast hits or affects a creature, you can move that creature up to 5 ft.
Violent Attraction: You can turn gravity into force. Reaction: add extra damage to an attack, or to falling damage, a few times per long rest.

Event Horizon: You create a field that drags enemies toward you and holds them in place. Once per long rest, or by spending 18 mana, a creature in the field must move toward you and cannot move on its turn.

Order of Scribes.about: Wizards who write the spells they learn into their own books, and who can copy a spell from any page. Scribes are the librarians of the mage-guilds and the keepers of its secrets.
features: A magical quill that copies spells quickly and cheaply.
Swap a spell's damage type for another from your book, and cast rituals faster.
Make your book's spirit appear and cast spells from its location.
Make a magic scroll of a spell you know after a long rest, cast as one level higher.
Advantage on Arcana checks, and let your book take damage for you by erasing spells temporarily.

Alchemist.about: You brew potions and elixirs, and you can heal and restore with the right mixture. Alchemists work in the apothecaries of [[Loreaon]] and the sea-chapels of the coast.
features: Proficiency with alchemist's supplies (or another artisan's tool if you have it).

After a long rest, make a random magic elixir in an empty flask: healing, swiftness, resilience, boldness, flight or transformation. Spend 5 mana to brew one you choose (10 for a second, and so on by spell cost). More free elixirs at 6th and 15th.
When you cast a spell through alchemist's supplies, add your Intelligence modifier to one roll of its acid, fire, necrotic or poison damage or its healing.
Your elixirs also give temporary hit points, and you can cast Lesser Restoration without mana a few times per long rest.
Resistance to acid and poison, immune to being poisoned, and once per long rest each cast Greater Restoration and Heal without mana or materials.

Armorer.about: You build armour that fights beside you, and you can turn a suit of steel into a second body. Armorers serve the knights and the garrisons who need their gear to hold.
features: Proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.
Your armor becomes your spell focus, can't be removed against your will, covers your whole body and can be donned in an action.
Guardian (thunder gauntlets that draw enemies to you, and temporary hit points as a bonus action) or Infiltrator (a lightning launcher, +5 speed and advantage on Stealth). Swap after a rest.
Attack twice when you take the Attack action.
Your armor counts as separate items for infusions (armor, helmet, boots, weapon), so you can infuse more of it.
Guardian: pull a Huge or smaller creature 30 feet toward you as a reaction and attack it. Infiltrator: creatures you hit glow and take extra lightning damage.

Artillerist.about: You build cannons, catapults and other engines of war, and you can turn a workshop into a battery. Artillerists are paid well by the armies and avoided by the cities they defend.
features: Build a small or tiny magical cannon once per long rest (or spend 5 mana for another): a flamethrower, force ballista or protector (temporary hit points for allies). Fire it as a bonus action.
Carve a wand, staff or rod into a firearm; spells cast through it deal an extra 1d8 damage.
Your cannons hit harder (+1d8), and you can detonate one as an action.
You can have two cannons at once, and allies near a cannon have half cover.

Battle Smith.about: You build a steel companion that fights at your side, and you keep it running in the thick of combat. Battle smiths are the mechanics of the knightly orders.
features: Proficiency with martial weapons, and use Intelligence for attacks and damage with magic weapons.
A loyal construct companion that fights on your turn, protects allies with its reaction and repairs itself. It grows with your level.
Attack twice when you take the Attack action.
When you or your defender hit, deal an extra 2d6 force damage or heal a creature within 30 feet for 2d6, a few times per long rest.
Arcane Jolt grows to 4d6, your defender gets +2 AC, and its deflections deal force damage back.

Order of the Ghostslayer.about: The oldest order: hunters of undead who wield sunlight and spirit. Ghostslayers are welcome in the churches and feared by the cults of the dead.
features: A new Crimson Rite that sheds light, gives resistance to necrotic damage, and deals extra damage to undead.
Extra uses of Blood Maledict, and you can amplify a curse without the hit point cost once per rest.
For a few rounds, become partly ghostly: walk through creatures and objects, fly or hover. Once per short or long rest.
Your brand weakens spirits and keeps a branded creature from becoming incorporeal; your hits on it deal extra damage.
A curse that ends being charmed, frightened or possessed on a creature, damaging the possessor.
When you drop to 0 hit points with a Crimson Rite active, you can end the rite to drop to 1 hit point instead, a few times per long rest.

Order of the Lycan.about: Hunters who take the wolf’s blood into themselves to fight the beasts of the night. Lycan hunters keep to the edges of the villages and serve as the last line of defence.
features: Advantage on Perception checks that use hearing or smell.

Turn into a half-wolf for an hour: stronger, faster, tougher against nonmagical weapons, with claws. You risk bloodlust when hurt (a Wisdom save to keep control). Once per short or long rest, more later.
Better speed and jumping, and your claws get better in hybrid form.
Your hybrid form heals itself each turn and its claws strike harder.
Better control of the bloodlust, and advantage on attacks against creatures you've branded.
Full control of the beast: more uses, a blood curse of the howl, and you can change at will.

Order of the Mutant.about: Hunters who reshape their bodies with the blood of monsters, and who are unafraid of what they become. Mutant hunters are hired for the dangerous jobs and paid well for the risk.
features: Learn mutagen formulas that boost one stat or sense at a cost (for example, stronger but slower). More formulas as you level.
After a rest, brew a number of mutagens; drink one as a bonus action. Their side effects last until your next rest.
Immune to poison damage and the poisoned condition, and you can ignore one mutagen's side effect once per long rest.
Your brand stops a creature changing shape or turning invisible, and dispels illusions on it.
A curse that poisons a creature, damaging it each turn.
Change one active mutagen's effect for another as a bonus action, once per short rest.

Order of the Profane Soul.about: Hunters who draw on dark pacts to fuel their blood and their blades. Profane hunters are hunted by the orders that disapprove of them.
features: Pick a patron (in Avarenth, one of the gods or demons). Your Crimson Rite and features take on its flavor.
You learn warlock spells and cast them with mana; your spellcasting ability is Intelligence. You start with two cantrips. Your list stops at 4th level like other half casters.
Your weapon is your spell focus while a Crimson Rite is active, and your patron gives your rite a small extra effect.
When you cast a cantrip as an action, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.
Once per long rest, cast one spell from your patron's list without spending mana.
A creature you've branded has disadvantage on saves against your spells. You also learn a curse that lets you feed on the dying to regain a little mana.
Once per long rest, cast a stronger spell your patron grants without spending mana.

_note: Short summaries written for Avarenth in our own words, not the book text. Check the exact wording in your copy of the book. Spell-slot costs are given in mana.
